metadata.title: Pick a Number, Any Number
metadata.purpose: One dataset can hand you four different true numbers. Two parties each got a menu. Both picked the highest one. Which number you quote is the whole argument, and the decimal point on it does the persuading. Nobody lies; everybody picks.
metadata.honesty_law: BINDING — see PLAN.md §HONESTY LAW. B09 carries the INFERENCE label on screen. 65% and 97.5% shown together in B04. 40% and 21.9% shown together in BRM. Three academic studies plus commercial reviews acknowledged in B09. Substack and Pangram named (Law 3a). Paper/authors/university NOT named (Law 3b).

beats.narration_text: Merhaba — this is Liam, in for Bear. One dataset can hand you four different true numbers. Two parties each got a menu. Both picked the highest one. Following what each chose — and what they passed over — is the whole film.

beats.narration_text: The report has four numbers. All true. All from the same scan. Thirteen point eight percent — the global average, all platforms. Twenty-one point nine percent — Substack's own combined rate; the report calls Substack an exception. Twenty-five point seven two percent — longform over two hundred and fifty words, all platforms, fully AI. Forty percent — LinkedIn longform, fully AI. The number the announcement used was the last one on that list.

beats.narration_text: Where does the platform's accuracy claim link to?

props.command: Where does the platform's accuracy claim link to?

beats.narration_text: Chris Best's post on Substack — 'Against Claudefishing,' twenty-first of July twenty twenty-six — says the tool is not perfect, but independent research suggests it detects AI-generated text with a high degree of accuracy. The link does not go to the research. It goes to Pangram's own evaluations page. And Pangram's self-reported false-positive rate of zero point zero one percent lives on that same page. Independent is doing unearned work at two separate hops. The companion video covers what a false-positive rate does and does not license.

beats.narration_text: Six numbers, all with decimal points: thirteen point eight, twenty-one point nine, twenty-five point seven two, sixty-five point zero, ninety-seven point five, zero point zero one. Precision was not the question. Selection was. The decimal does rhetorical work the measurement never authorised.

beats.narration_text: Nobody lied. The platform reached past the two numbers about Substack — its own rate of twenty-one point nine percent, the global average of thirteen point eight — to the highest figure in the report. The vendor reached past sixty-five percent strict to ninety-seven point five inclusive. Both true. Both chosen. A chain that loses a qualifier per hop needs no bad actor at any link. It needs only someone, at each address, to reach for the number that sounds best.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. The prompt: take a statistic you've quoted recently — trace it back one source at a time until you reach the people who measured it, and tell me what qualifier fell off at each step. This is a five-minute habit. And this film gives you a place to start: Substack's post and Pangram's evaluations page are both named and live. You can run the trace right now.
